message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
It includes both the `gcloud` CLI command (the easiest way) and the equivalent **REST API** payload you could POST to the Compute Engine endpoint if you prefer to work directly with the API.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project (`PROJECT_ID`) with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled for that project.  
> * You need the **NVIDIA A6000** GPU family available in the zone you choose.  
> * Your account must have the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent).  
> * The `gcloud` SDK must be installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  

---

## 1️⃣ Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports A6000 GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \   # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
    --boot-disk-size=200GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000 \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: custom init script
    --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Size & performance of the boot disk. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Selects the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs at first boot (e.g., install drivers). |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules if you plan to expose services. |

> 📌 **Tip** – If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, just change the `count` and `type` fields accordingly.

---

## 2️⃣ Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom application), you can POST the following JSON payload to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-balanced",
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### How to send the request

1. **Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token** with scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
2. Include it in the header: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN`.  
3. Send the POST request (e.g., via `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client library).

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

> 🔧 **Note** – The `guestAccelerators` field is what tells Compute Engine to attach the GPU.  
> The `initializeParams.sourceImage` points to the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family.

---

## 3️⃣ After Creation

Once the instance is running:

1. **SSH into the VM** (via `gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu` or the Cloud Console SSH button).  
2. Verify the GPU is detected:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with driver version 535.x (or newer).  

3. Install any additional software you need (CUDA, cuDNN, TensorFlow, PyTorch, etc.).

---

## 4️⃣ Cleanup

When you’re done, delete the instance to avoid incurring charges:

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete rtx-a6000-ubuntu --project=my-gcp-project --zone=us-central1-a
```

Or via REST:

```bash
DELETE https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances/rtx-a6000-ubuntu
```

---

### Quick Reference Table

| Action | CLI Command | REST Endpoint |
|--------|-------------|---------------|
| Create instance | `gcloud compute instances create ...` | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/.../instances` |
| Delete instance | `gcloud compute instances delete ...` | `DELETE https://compute.googleapis.com/.../instances/{NAME}` |
| List instances | `gcloud compute instances list` | `GET https://compute.googleapis.com/.../instances` |

Feel free to copy the snippets above, adjust the variables, and run them in your environment. Happy GPU computing!
